  3. The generic Odin ABI for the engine boundary

#The generic Odin ABI for the engine boundary

Status: prototype (native/js/odin_abi/), a separate trunk that does not touch the main build. It shows the guest ↔ host boundary built by Odin's compile-time generics from shared Odin declarations, with no code generator — the plan Sacha set on 28/10 ("GARDER LE WASM"): the engine stays a Wasm module, the boundary becomes a small generic ABI, and the only tool that remains extracts the documentation and the conformance report.

#Why

Today src/tools/bindgen reads api/*.widl (~5 000 lines of Odin) and writes ~40 000 lines: the host trampolines (src/page/api_generated.odin), the Odin guest SDK (sdk/odin/web/*), the C guest header (native/js/gen/wren_api.h), the docs and the conformance cases. Every function has one hand-shaped Wasm import and one hand-shaped host trampoline. It is fast, but it is a generator: a second language to parse (.widl), emit and keep in step with the engine.

When the engine is written in Odin (wasm32), both ends of the boundary can read the same Odin declarations and let the compiler instantiate the bridges. No .widl, no emitted C, no emitted Odin. One source of truth; a shape mismatch becomes a compile error instead of a silent ABI drift.

#Shape of the boundary

Two wire shapes, one serialisation and one set of compile-time marshallers (package abi). Both ends read package api_decl, so the host and the wasm32 guest agree by construction.

#1. The scalar fast path (hot)

Each argument stays a separate Wasm scalar in the call's raw cell array, decoded by a constant index; a string result goes into a (ptr, cap) buffer and the call returns the length needed. This is byte-for-byte the current wr_* ABI (handles i64, strings (ptr, len), errors a negative i32), but the trampoline is built by the compiler from the signature (abi_host.register_scalar_*) instead of generated. It carries the hot 0..N simple-parameter functions (getters, setters, numeric calls).

#2. The serialised path (general, cold)

One import per domain, host_call(op, args_ptr, args_len, ret_ptr, ret_cap) -> status. The guest packs the arguments into its own memory and names the function by an operation number; the host validates the two spans against the module's memory, decodes the arguments against the declaration, calls the implementation, and serialises the result into the result buffer. A result that does not fit returns Truncated; the guest grows its buffer and retries. This carries the shapes the fixed cell array cannot (long argument lists, growable results) and keeps the import table small. It costs one copy per argument plus one indirect dispatch — about +100 ns/call over the scalar path (measured below), so it is not used for the hot getters.

Both shapes exist because the measurement shows the serialised path is too expensive for the hottest functions, and the scalar path cannot express everything (a 28-argument URLPattern constructor, a growable getAll).

#Serialisation

Little-endian, no padding (the only byte order wasm32 and the host use), self-describing by static type:

Odin typewire
bool, i32, enum (i32)4 bytes
i64, u64, a handle (distinct abi.Handle)8 bytes
f648 bytes
stringu32 length, then the bytes; the host checks UTF-8
[]u8 / abi.Bytesu32 length, then the bytes; no check
Maybe(string)length == 0xFFFF_FFFF (ABSENT) when absent, else as a string
Maybe(T) otherwisea u8 present-flag, then the value
a dictionary (struct)its fields in declaration order (see "Out of scope")

The result is the status cell followed by the return values in the same format. Reading and writing is a cursor (abi.Reader / abi.Writer); a read past the end sets a flag the dispatcher turns into a trap, a write past ret_cap sets Truncated and the length needed.

#The declarations (package api_decl)

One package both the host and the guest import (when ODIN_ARCH == .wasm32 on the guest). It expresses:

  • handles as distinct types (URL :: distinct abi.Handle), so the compiler keeps a URL from being passed where a URLSearchParams is wanted; on the wire a handle is a u64, resolved to the live object by the host binding;
  • enumerations (i32);
  • dictionaries as structs with default values, an absent member told apart by its has_* flag;
  • procedure signatures (the arguments and the result), with raises expressed as an abi.Api_Error last return value, and ownership noted in the doc comment ([Owned] → the caller releases; a borrowed handle is called out).

The signatures carry no context: the host binds an implementation of shape proc(ctx: ^Call, <args>) -> <result> and the guest a stub of shape proc(<args>) -> <result>; the bridge adds or drops the context. abi_host.bind checks at compile time that the implementation is the declaration plus a leading context, same returns.

#The bridges (compile-time, base:intrinsics)

The crux is that Odin can walk a procedure type at compile time: type_proc_parameter_count, type_proc_parameter_type(P, <const>), type_proc_return_count, type_proc_return_type, type_is_enum, type_base_type, type_is_union + type_variant_type_of (for Maybe). Two constraints shaped the design:

  • type_proc_parameter_type(P, i) needs a constant index and is a type only inside a procedure body, not in a signature. So the per-argument decode is written inline in an arity ladder (0..8 arguments after the context), one branch per parameter count; each branch decodes exactly its arguments and calls the implementation. The ladder is the whole "generic" cost, written once.
  • a proc "c" Wasm callback cannot capture locals. The host trampoline is produced by a generic (register_scalar_* / bind → install) that captures the implementation value at compile time, so the stored trampoline closes over nothing at run time; the registry is reached through one process-global pointer and a specialised thunk.

Result encoding is by procedure overloading (encode_returns): void, a value, an Api_Error, or (value, Api_Error) — the compiler picks the form from the call's return tuple, no run-time test. There is no reflection on the hot path: every decode_arg / encode_ret resolves at compile time to the right load, check and store for that exact type.

#Measurements

Machine: the author's Windows box, Cranelift (speed), wasm32 guest over Wasmtime, 1 M calls each, median of 3 (native/js/odin_abi/bench). The scalar "hand-written" column is a proc "c" written exactly as bindgen emits it, registered next to the comptime bridges under a sibling module, so all three are the same machine, engine and guest.

shapewr_* scalar (hand-written / generated)scalar bridge (comptime)serialised host_call (comptime)
URLSearchParams_size (handle → i32)~50 ns/call~62 ns/call~150 ns/call
URL_get .Pathname (handle, enum → string)~135 ns/call~150 ns/call~245 ns/call

Readings:

  • The comptime scalar bridge matches the generated trampoline (within ~12 ns, from the one extra indirection to the config holder, which a real package page integration inlines through api_begin). The import structure confirms it: the guest's scalar calls are per-function imports, exactly as wr_* today; the serialised path is a single host_call import.
  • The serialised path costs ~+100 ns/call: the per-argument copy and one indirect dispatch into the op table. Fine for constructors and cold functions, too much for the hottest getters — hence keeping the scalar path.

An in-process check (native/js/odin_abi/check, no Wasm instance, the exact guest bindings against the dispatcher) exercises the whole domain (parse, getters, relative resolution, searchParams both-way link, the URLPattern dictionary constructor, test()), each result checked against the native wb:url.

#Proof: two domains end to end

native/js/odin_abi/ migrates the URL / URLSearchParams / URLPattern domain of api/url.widl end to end:

  • api_decl/url.odin — the shared declarations (handles, enums, the URLPatternInit dictionary, 18 procedure signatures with raises).
  • abi_url/ — the host implementation, backed by the real wb:url, with its own handle pools (standalone so the prototype does not entangle package page). build_registry binds each declaration to its implementation; URLPattern_create uses the dictionary escape hatch (bind_manual).
  • abi_guest/guest_url.odin — the guest bindings (the mirror of the shipped SDK), the same code that compiles to wasm32.
  • bench_guest/ + bench/ — the wasm32 guest and the host runner for the measurement.
  • check/ — the in-process round-trip, all assertions passing.

The engine today is QuickJS in C, so a real integration also needs a thin C guest that calls host_call (the shape is one import plus a serialise/deserialise helper); that is the native/js/runtime glue, coordinated with the C↔Odin work. The Odin guest path above is what the boundary becomes once the engine is Odin.

#The tool that remains

apidoc (native/js/odin_abi/apidoc) reads package api_decl with core:odin/parser + core:odin/ast and writes one Markdown page per module (docs/api/<module>.md): the handles, enumerations, dictionaries and function signatures with their doc comments — what bindgen produced from .widl. The conformance report is the same walk (the inventory of declared functions, their arguments and whether they raise). This is the only generator-like step left, and it reads the Odin declarations, not a second language.

#Migration plan, domain by domain

  1. Shared declarations. For each api/<domain>.widl, write api_decl/<domain>.odin: handles, enums, dictionaries, procedure signatures. (This replaces the .widl as the source of truth; bindgen can emit it once as a starting point, then .widl is dropped.)
  2. Host. Move the hand-written implementation (today in src/page/bindings_<domain>.odin) to take the declaration's arguments; bind each with abi_host.bind (scalar or serialised) in the domain's registry. The implementations keep using package page (its object pool, settings, lookups) — the standalone abi_url here is only to keep the prototype off the main build.
  3. Guest. The guest bindings become the abi_guest stubs (or, for the C engine during the transition, the C glue over host_call).
  4. Choose the path per function. Scalar for the hot 0..N simple-parameter functions (the budget check in perf.ps1 tells which); serialised for the rest.
  5. Docs/conformance come from apidoc on the new declarations; delete the .widl and the matching bindgen emitters once a domain is across.
  6. Repeat; bindgen shrinks to nothing but the one-shot .widl → api_decl helper, then goes away with the last domain.

#Out of scope for the compile-time bridge (and how to express it)

  • Dictionaries with strings (URLPatternInit): the generic marshaller stays pure (scalars, strings, handles, Maybe); a dictionary is carried by the manual escape hatch (abi_host.bind_manual), a small hand-written codec that reads the fields with the same wire helpers. Dictionaries are constructor/option-bag arguments, off the hot path, so this costs nothing in practice. A future improvement is a comptime struct-field walk, but it is not needed.
  • WebIDL overloads (foo(DOMString) and foo(long) as one name): Web IDL only; resolved in the engine's JS glue by dispatching to two differently-named ABI functions, as today.
  • Unions ((DOMString or Blob)): expressed as a tag enum plus the per-variant arguments, or a manual op.
  • [Exposed] / realms (Window vs Worker): a bit on the binding, as today (realms on wasm.Import); set when binding, filtered by the worker import filter.
  • Mixins / inheritance: a Web IDL authoring convenience; the declarations are already flat (one function per line), so there is nothing to express.
  • Callbacks (an event listener handed to the host): a table index + a user word, unchanged; call_guest runs them. Not part of the argument marshalling.

#Files

native/js/odin_abi/
  abi/            abi.odin wire.odin marshal.odin invoke.odin   -- the wire format + the comptime marshallers
  abi_host/       host.odin dispatch.odin scalar.odin           -- the host bridge (bind/install, host_call, scalar)
  abi_guest/      guest.odin host_call.odin guest_url.odin      -- the guest transport + the URL bindings
  api_decl/       url.odin                                      -- the shared declarations
  abi_url/        host.odin impl.odin                           -- the URL domain implementation (real wb:url)
  bench_guest/    main.odin scalar.odin cm_scalar.odin          -- the wasm32 benchmark guest
  bench/          main.odin scalar_baseline.odin                -- the Wasmtime benchmark runner
  check/          main.odin                                     -- the in-process round-trip check
  apidoc/         main.odin                                     -- docs/conformance from api_decl (core:odin/parser)
